top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Tartu Rattaralli's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
Tartu Rattaralli's flat-fast with rolling kicks rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.

Road-specific control matters at Tartu Rattaralli. Practice on flat-fast with rolling kicks: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 81 miles.
At mile 60 of 81, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Tartu Rattaralli. Train it until it feels boring.
At Tartu Rattaralli, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
When someone attacks on flat-fast with rolling kicks, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Tartu Rattaralli. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on flat-fast with rolling kicks can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 81 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,858ft of climbing on flat-fast with rolling kicks does to your power file on race day.
Varied gradients on flat-fast with rolling kicks demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.

race_overlay.weather: June in Tartu, South Estonia, Estonia — Early June in Tartu brings mild temps around 15-22°C with long daylight for endless pedaling. Expect variable Baltic breezes but generally rider-friendly conditions. Rain is possible but rarely race-ruining. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Tartu Rattaralli. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Tartu Rattaralli’s 81 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Tartu Rattaralli rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on flat-fast with rolling kicks to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, TT Threshold, and Road Specific to prepare you for 81 miles of flat-fast with rolling kicks in Tartu, South Estonia, Estonia.
